shopify.text: Native. A market is a set of customers the merchant defines: countries or regions, company locations (B2B), retail locations or channels. The page states no per-plan market count.

criteria: A store lists the countries it sells to as markets, each with its own currency, default language, shipping rate, VAT rate and prices.
A market address is {country}[-{lang}][-{currency}] and a language or currency the store does not offer is not found.
A visitor's country is matched to the store's market for a suggestion; a country the store does not sell to gives none.

gap: Availability is implied by a price row (the product editor says: leave a country empty to not sell there); there is no catalog object, no per-market switch that keeps the price, and no per-market product set shared across countries.
criteria: An owner can switch a product (or a variant) off in one market without deleting its price, and back on.
A product switched off in a market is absent from that market's listings, search, product page, chat, sitemap and structured data, and a cart line for it is refused.
The switch is read by cartSummary() and placeOrder() alike, and a checkout-kinds scenario (euro view included) holds that they agree.
A store copy (duplicate_store) carries the availability.

feature: Fixed per-market prices and adjustment rules
gap: Prices are entered by hand per country (and converted per D109 when shown in another currency, rounded to the store's step); there is no percentage rule per market and no bulk adjustment.
criteria: An owner sets a market rule (percentage up or down, rounding step) that derives that market's prices from a base price; a fixed price on a product overrides the rule.
Derived prices are written through commerce.set_price, so prior_30d_minor and the 30-day reference stay genuine.
A bulk change over a chosen set of products shows a preview (old and new price) before it is applied and is written to the audit log.
A euro-view scenario in checkout-kinds.int.test.ts holds that the shown price equals the charged price.

gap: Path-per-market (/s/{store}/{market}) and up to 5 domains per store with one primary (P7, P8); a market cannot have its own domain or ccTLD, so no.example.com and de.example.com cannot be set per country.
criteria: An owner assigns a domain (or subdomain) to a market, verified like the store's domains, and the market's pages are served on it.
The other addresses of that market redirect to its domain, and hreflang and canonical links point to the chosen domain of each market.
Links built by paths.ts, emails and Stripe return URLs use the market's domain.
A store with no per-market domain behaves exactly as today.
A store offers any language from the platform's registry, independent of its countries, and a shopper chooses language and currency apart.
Interface text falls back to English key by key; Norwegian, Swedish, Danish and English are hand-written, other languages are AI-translated into data and read by key.
Products, menus and pages are translated in one run, a person ticks each suggestion before it is saved, legal texts start unticked and pages are saved as drafts.
Every AI translation passes validation (shape, length, claims filter) and the product, page and store texts fall back to the main language when no translation exists.

gap: A store's pages, menus and product texts vary by language, not by country: a German-speaking shopper in Austria and in Germany sees the same page. Only campaigns can be limited to some countries (D116).
criteria: A page, row or block can be limited to chosen markets (countries) and is not drawn, and not in the sitemap, for the others.
A product text or a menu can differ by market on top of its language, falling back to the language's text.
The builder shows which market a visitor view is for, and the store translation worklist counts per-market overrides.
A shopper sees prices in a currency the store offers at the store's rate (ECB rates refreshed daily when automatic), rounded to the store's step.
Amounts are stored in the country's own currency; what is shown is converted when read and what is written (order, subscription, delivery) is in nativeCurrency.
cartSummary() and placeOrder() agree in the euro view (checkout-kinds scenario).
A currency with no rate is not offered.

shopify.text: Native. Rounding to each currency's most common denominator; the page says rules cannot be customised, and only stores on Shopify Payments can use it.

criteria: A converted amount is rounded to a multiple of the store's step per currency (0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10 in major units), with a default per currency (HUF whole forints).
Rounding applies to the shown and the charged amount alike.

gap: A visitor's country (x-vercel-ip-country) is suggested only on the store's country chooser; no banner or popup on other pages, and it never redirects, by design (Geo-blocking Regulation).
criteria: A visitor whose country has a market other than the one shown sees a dismissible suggestion on any store page, linking to that market on the same page.
The suggestion never redirects and is not shown to crawlers; dismissal is kept only after consent (KNOWN_COOKIES entry) or in memory.
A country the store does not sell to gets no suggestion; the text is in the shopper's language.

gap: Unit 1a (D157 proposed) built criteria 1, 2 and the 'off and says why' half of 4: a store records its IOSS number (`IM` plus ten digits), the intermediary's name, the markets it applies to and the registration date (`commerce.store_tax_profile`, `/admin/{store}/settings/tax`); a consignment of at most 150.00 EUR sent from outside the EU to a private buyer in a listed EU market is charged destination VAT and the order records `vat_kind = 'ioss'` and the number; above 150 EUR (`ioss_over_limit`), for a business buyer, outside the listed markets, from an EU dispatch country, for downloads, or where the currency has no euro rate it is not an IOSS sale; without a number or markets the screen says IOSS is off and what it needs. Unit 1b's invoice carries the IOSS statement and the number (D159). Unit 1c (D161 proposed) built criterion 3: `/admin/{store}/analytics/tax?view=ioss` gives the monthly IOSS data per Member State of consumption and rate in euro at the ECB's reference rate of the month's last day (or the owner's audited override), as a formula-safe CSV, refused while a rate is missing, with the above-150 EUR and other unmarked orders listed with their reason and a next-month credit note as a Part 3 correction (`tax-reports.int.test.ts` IOSS scenario, `oss-return.test.ts`, `tax-csv.test.ts`, `tax-report-admin.int.test.ts`, `oss-view.test.ts`), and the off-and-says-why state is rendered. Still short of Full: (1) bucket B: live only with a registered IOSS number or intermediary agreement the owner holds, which nothing here checks, and Kaizen submits no IOSS return; (2) the 150 EUR test uses the basket's shipped lines, not a proper intrinsic-value definition (not read), and the EU's removal of the customs-duty exemption from 1 July 2026 (Shopify's page, read 2026-10-03) is not handled; (3) the IOSS statement, the import notice, the admin help text and the report's part-of-return rules are hand-written, unreviewed and need a tax accountant (including whether a Norwegian store may register directly, marked verify); (4) neither the tax screen nor the IOSS view was opened in a browser with data (render and action tests only).
criteria: A store can record an IOSS identification number (and its intermediary) and the markets it applies to.
A consignment of at most 150 EUR sent from outside the EU into an EU market is charged destination VAT at checkout and the order records the IOSS number; above 150 EUR it is not an IOSS sale.
A monthly IOSS report per member state and rate can be exported.
Live only with a registered IOSS number or intermediary agreement (bucket B); until then the feature is off and says why.

history.why: Unit 1a (docs/wave-1a-tax.md): read the code and ran ioss, tax-profile and vat-engine tests: the IOSS number, intermediary and markets are recorded, an order of at most 150 EUR from outside the EU is marked IOSS in the cart and order, above 150 EUR and every other case is not, the screen says what is missing. Kept partial and not Full: the monthly IOSS report (1c) and the invoice marking (1b) do not exist, and bucket B needs a registration the owner holds.

feature: Customs duties, HS codes, landed cost
gap: Variants store an HS code and country of origin (validated digits); nothing is calculated: no duty or import VAT estimate, no DDP quote at checkout, no customs data on documents.
criteria: For a shipment from the store's origin to a destination outside its customs area, checkout shows an estimated duty and import VAT (landed cost) from a duty-rate source, or says it cannot.
The estimate comes from the variant's HS code and origin and is the same in the cart and the placed order (euro scenario in checkout-kinds).
The order keeps the duties and VAT collected and who pays (DDP or DAP) and customs data reaches the carrier booking where the carrier takes it.
A missing HS code blocks a DDP quote with a plain message, never a zero duty.

feature: Legal page templates and policy generator
gap: Built and tested, not Full, because no person has read the texts and nothing here may be called Full on the strength of hand-written legal text alone (docs/parity/WAVES.md step 4). Starters for terms, privacy, returns, shipping, withdrawal information and an imprint exist in nb, sv, da and en (src/lib/legal-starters/*), are filled from legalFacts(), are made as drafts with a review notice and [[placeholders]] that the builder's checker blocks publishing over, and stay out of the sitemap until published. Checkout shows a terms and privacy link or a required checkbox (stores.terms_at_checkout) and the pay press records order_terms with immutable legal_snapshots. Missing: (1) a person's review of every text, and the eight questions in docs/wave-1-trust.md section 8 (the pay button's wording under CRD Art. 8(2), the durable-medium duty, guarantee periods and complaint bodies per country, the Swedish and Danish statutes, the privacy starter's recipients and transfers); (2) the checkout sentence, tick box and recording are held by component and integration tests only: the demo store takes no payments, so no end-to-end run reaches the pay button; (3) the order confirmation email does not link the accepted terms yet (the lead adds the line at merge), and orders confirmed wholly at the venue and subscription renewals have no sentence and no record; (4) the goods exclusions are printed for every store with a [[Check]] line rather than filtered by what the store sells, and a translation made stale by a later edit of the main text is still shown as it was (D55). The migrations legal_terms and legal_terms_rules are not yet applied to production. Skeptic check (2026-10-03): (5) the sitemap clause of criterion 4 (a draft starter is left out until published) is held only indirectly: e2e/legal-pages.spec.ts says in a comment that it does not check the sitemap, and legal-starters.int.test.ts asserts only that a legal page is not in the list of role pages kept out of the sitemap; no test reads the sitemap output with a draft and a published starter. (6) The tick box in checkbox mode is enforced in the browser only: recordTermsAcceptance() runs before Stripe's confirm and the browser does not start the payment when it fails, but nothing on the server refuses to complete an order that has no order_terms record (staff are only shown the missing record), so a client that skips the page's script pays without ticking.
criteria: A store can create starter pages for privacy, terms, shipping, returns and withdrawal information and an imprint, in nb, sv, da and en, filled from the store's business details and settings (return window, who pays return shipping).
Every starter is hand-written, marked draft and carries a visible notice that it needs legal review before use; none is machine-translated.
Checkout can show a terms and privacy link (or a required checkbox when the owner chooses) that points to the store's chosen pages and records the acceptance on the order.
A starter is never published automatically and is left out of the sitemap until the owner publishes it.

history.why: Read src/lib/legal-starters/{nb,sv,da,en}.ts, src/lib/checkout-terms.ts, src/server/checkout-terms.ts and the order page; ran legal-starters.test.ts, checkout-terms.test.ts, legal-roles.test.ts, src/db/trust.test.ts, legal-starters.int.test.ts, checkout-terms.int.test.ts (all pass). All four criteria are built and held by tests; kept Partial because every text is hand-written and unreviewed (docs/wave-1-trust.md section 8) and the checkout sentence was never run against a live Stripe checkout

criteria: Every cookie or storage item a site sets is listed in KNOWN_COOKIES with category and purpose; a site that sets only necessary ones shows no banner, only a Cookies page.
A site using an optional category (a tracking tool) asks first, loads third-party scripts only after consent, and re-asks when the categories change.
Each choice is logged (commerce.consents, 12 months) through /api/consent; the Cookies page lists what the latest scan found.

gap: A shopper can delete their own account (details, password, picture, sessions, standing orders go; orders stay but lose the account link), but order rows keep name, address and email; there is no export of a customer's data (only custom-field values have customerFieldExport()), no staff-triggered erase or anonymise with the bookkeeping exceptions, and no retention schedule.
criteria: Staff (and the shopper from My account) can download a customer's data as a machine-readable file: profile, addresses, orders and lines, returns, consents, wishlists, reviews-to-be, custom-field values, emails sent.

Staff can erase a customer on request: the account and personal fields go, and orders under the bookkeeping duty are anonymised or restricted (name, address, email removed after the retention period) with the reason logged in the audit log.
A retention schedule (orders, emails, search queries, carts) runs from the cron and a test shows what it removes and what it keeps.
Another store's data is never in an export (multi-tenant test); the export and the erasure are audit-logged.

feature: EU withdrawal function and self-service returns

shopify.text: Native, partly. Shopify's page says merchants can use Shopify's return and cancellation rules to help meet the electronic withdrawal function requirement, and must set up the clearly labelled button or link, two-step confirmation and email confirmations themselves; Managed Markets orders get compliant policies automatically. No plan tiers are named. Apps also sell a withdrawal button.

history.why: D153 shipped the function: /withdraw in two steps with a confirmation (unconfirmed requests expire in 24 hours), the same reply for a wrong email or order number, an acknowledgement email on a durable medium (stored in email_messages, retried by the job), returns with a forward-only lifecycle, a staff queue and refund through refundOrder(), the 14-day clock from recorded receipt, and shopper status pages. Read the code and the integration, unit and e2e tests (returns*.int.test.ts, withdrawal.test.ts, e2e/withdrawal.spec.ts).

criteria: A shopper withdraws at /s/{store}/{market}/withdraw in two steps (Withdraw from contract here, then Confirm withdrawal) without giving a reason; nothing is a withdrawal until the second step, and an unconfirmed request expires after 24 hours.
The reply is the same for a wrong email, an unknown order number and another store's order, and requests are limited by hashed keys, never by IP.
Confirming records the statement, creates a return and sends an acknowledgement on a durable medium with date and time; a failed email never undoes the withdrawal and is retried.

Eligibility and the 14-day period come only from lineEligibility() and withdrawalWindow(); the period counts from a recorded receipt, never an estimate, and excluded goods, companies, digital content and copied orders are refused with a reason.

Staff work a queue (receive, inspect, refund through refundOrder()); the refund amount comes only from refundFor() and never exceeds what was captured; a withdrawal return is never declined or cancelled.
Known limits, stated in docs/returns.md and not counted here: texts need human legal review; no carrier return labels, exchanges, or photos (separate rows).

shopify.text: App. Shopify's own withdrawal page says nothing about exclusions or a digital-content waiver. Apps such as EU Withdrawal Form let merchants exclude items (hygiene, personalised) and the listing does not mention a digital waiver; community threads say the waiver checkbox needs checkout customisation, which Shopify Basic does not allow.

criteria: Each variant carries one of the statutory exclusions (custom made, perishable, sealed hygiene, sealed media, mixed inseparably, price fluctuation, alcohol for future delivery, periodicals, digital content, dated service) or none, and the product editor offers them.
A download is bought only after the shopper ticks the digital-content consent at checkout; the consent time is stored on the order and the lines become digital_content.
The withdrawal function refuses an excluded line with its reason (sealed goods keep the right until unsealed) and never refuses a line that has the right.

gap: Criteria 1 to 3 are built and tested; criterion 4 is outside code, so this row stays Partial. e2e/a11y.spec.ts runs axe (WCAG 2.0 A to 2.2 AA) in light and dark over the storefront and the admin's sign-in, forgot-password and sign-up pages and fails on serious or critical findings, with a known-bad fixture proving it can fail; the statement generator (src/lib/a11y-statement.ts, /admin/{store}/settings/accessibility) makes a draft page in nb, sv, da and en that says "not assessed" until the owner records an audit; theme colour pairs are flagged below 4.5:1. Missing: (1) the independent audit, which is bucket D and never counted by code; (2) the Stripe payment form and the signed-in admin screens are not scanned in CI (no Stripe or Supabase session there), and the manual axe run on a test-mode checkout recorded in docs/pci.md has not been done; (3) an automated scan finds only part of the problems; (4) ENFORCEMENT_BODIES are all verified:false, the Annex V content was not read in full, and the statement text needs legal review (docs/wave-1-trust.md section 8). The e2e specs were run in this wave on a port other than 3100. Skeptic check (2026-10-03): no e2e renders the checkout page itself. a11y.spec.ts's checkout test only follows the demo store's redirect to the cart (the demo takes no payments) and scans the cart, and csp.spec.ts reads the checkout's headers only, so the checkout's own markup (address, delivery choice, terms sentence and tick box, pay button) is not scanned by axe at all, in addition to Stripe's form; the manual run recorded nowhere is therefore the only check of it.
criteria: CI runs an automated WCAG check over the storefront's front, product, cart, order, account (signed out) and withdraw pages, the checkout in the states reachable without a payment session, and the admin's signed-out entry pages, in light and dark where the theme allows, and fails on serious or critical violations. The payment form and signed-in admin screens are checked by hand and recorded.

A store can generate an accessibility statement from a template (conformance status, known issues, contact, enforcement body per country) in nb, sv, da and en, marked as needing review before publication.
Theme settings that fail the AA contrast ratio are refused or flagged in the theme editor (already partly true, held by a test).
Outside this row, and never counted as Full by code: an independent audit result.
A product cannot be active without a manufacturer (name, postal and electronic address, country) and, when the manufacturer is outside the EU, an EU responsible person.
Safety information is stored per language on the listing and shown on the product page.
The database refuses to activate a product that lacks these, and the editor says why before saving; downloads need none.

gap: Schemes are tracked per product and registrations per market (product_schemes, producer_registrations) and the SQL view commerce.missing_registrations lists what is unregistered, but there is no admin screen to enter schemes or registrations, nothing reads the view in the app, and nothing blocks selling a product whose scheme has no registration.
criteria: An owner records producer-responsibility registrations (scheme, market, number, valid from and to) in the admin and tags products with schemes.
A product under a scheme with no valid registration in a market cannot be bought there: it is refused in the cart and in placeOrder() with a plain reason, and staff see a list of what is blocked.
The registration number is shown where the law asks (the product page or documents) and a registration that expires blocks sales from the next day.
The unregistered view is covered by a test through the app's reader, not only in SQL.

shopify.text: Native. Merchants enter a total measurement and optional base measure per product or variant; the unit price shows on product, collection, cart, checkout and order-confirmation notifications; Online Store 2.0 themes need no change. The page notes it is a legal requirement in some regions, that the unit type is the same across all markets, and that some units (t, cg, st) are not offered.

gap: No field, display or structured data: variants carry no content or measure and the storefront shows no price per kg, litre or metre (Price Indication Directive; Norwegian rules).
criteria: A variant can carry a total measure and unit (g, kg, ml, l, cm, m, m2, piece) and a reference quantity (default 1 kg, 1 l, 1 m, 1 m2, 1 piece, or 100 g and 100 ml where allowed).

The product page, listing cards, cart, checkout and order confirmation show the unit price with the shown VAT treatment, converted per market currency like the price, and computed in code from the shown price.
A reduced price shows the unit price of the price charged; the 30-day reference is not misused for it.
Unit price appears in the product's JSON-LD (unitPricingMeasure and unitPricingBaseMeasure) and a unit price is refused when the measure is missing for a category the owner marked as requiring it.
A euro-view scenario in checkout-kinds.int.test.ts holds that the unit price shown equals the one computed from the charged price.

gap: Kaizen asks Stripe for MobilePay on every store's account (D23) and Stripe shows it in Denmark and Finland where the account qualifies; Vipps (Norway) and Swish are in private preview at Stripe, not available for Accounts v2, so Vipps cannot be offered, and an owner cannot see or switch the method from Kaizen.
criteria: Every store account requests MobilePay and the admin shows per method whether it is on and why not (requirements), already true for MobilePay.
When Stripe opens Vipps to Kaizen's platform account, the capability is requested and the method is offered to Norwegian shoppers without code outside the payment list.
A payment-method switch per market is shown in the admin and never uses payment_method_types.
Live only after Stripe grants access (bucket B); alternatively through a second payment provider if the strategy decision allows it.

shopify.text: App. Not confirmed: searching Shopify's help centre, community and app store found no Brønnøysund company lookup; the Norwegian right of withdrawal falls under the EU withdrawal page's apps and rules. Tier left as app from memory.

criteria: A Norwegian organisation number (mod-11 checked before any call) or a company name fills a Work client's or a shop company account's legal name, address and VAT number from Enhetsregisteret; only the typed number or words are sent and nothing is saved from the lookup.
Norway's right of withdrawal (angrerettloven section 22) is served by the same withdrawal function as the EU's (D153).

gap: Database and functions are pinned to Ireland and Dublin (D10, vercel.json) and every vendor is listed in docs/residency-register.md, but the register shows DPAs for Supabase, Vercel, Resend, OpenAI and the gateway as still to accept in the vendors' dashboards, and OpenAI (api.openai.com, US) and Resend's account data and logs are outside the EU.
criteria: Every vendor that touches personal data is in docs/residency-register.md with region and DPA status before production use.
AI calls go to an EU-pinned provider or the store is told they do not (the provider's region is shown on the AI settings page).
Outside code: each DPA accepted and recorded with date; a sub-processor list a store can show its customers.

shopify.text: Native. shopify.com/security states Shopify is certified Level 1 PCI DSS compliant; the compliance reports help page lets logged-in merchants view Shopify's PCI Attestation of Compliance.

gap: Criteria 1 to 4 are built and held by tests at the level of the header, the import graph and the components; Partial because the attestation is the company's and the policy was never run against a live Stripe payment. src/lib/csp.ts sends an enforced Content-Security-Policy on cart, checkout and order of every store (both address shapes; no unsafe-eval; Stripe's origins as its guide lists them), OffPayRoutes draws no consent manager, owner code, chat widget or affiliate capture there, the pages are entered by full page loads (PayRouteGuard), the checkout page may not hold an HTML or embedded-video block, and no-card-fields.test.ts scans for card inputs. Missing: (1) the SAQ A attestation, and the question whether Kaizen as platform has PCI duties of its own (docs/pci.md; the company's, bucket D); (2) the manual test-mode payment on a preview through to the order page, with the console open and an axe run, is not done (the table in docs/pci.md is empty), so it is not known that Stripe's form, redirect methods and address autocomplete (https://maps.googleapis.com was added from Stripe's guide, never seen working) work under the enforced policy; CSP_ENFORCE = false is the one-line fallback; (3) script-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' because the prerendered shell cannot carry a nonce, so the policy stops other origins' scripts but not an injected inline one (the SRI form was not tried); (4) e2e/csp.spec.ts "the cart loads under the policy with no violation" FAILS on the current tree (re-run 2026-10-03): the review fix made PayRouteGuard import @/lib/affiliates, which imports zod, whose JIT probe calls Function("") and the browser reports it as a securitypolicyviolation (script-src blocked eval); harmless at runtime (zod falls back) but it puts the violation back on cart, checkout and order until withAffiliate() is moved out of the zod module or zod is set to jitless; (5) the migrations are not applied and nothing is deployed.
criteria: Card details are entered only in Stripe's payment form on Kaizen's checkout page (Stripe Elements, ui_mode elements) or on Stripe's hosted pages; no Kaizen route receives, logs or stores a card number, expiry or security code.
Payments are direct charges on the store's connected account, so the card data's scope is Stripe's (SAQ A style).
A strict Content-Security-Policy is sent on the checkout, order and cart routes (test of the header).
`liveCustomCode()`, `ConsentManager` scripts and the chat widget are not drawn on checkout routes, and a test fails if a checkout route imports them.

history.why: No CSP; the chat widget and owner/tracking scripts load on /checkout, against the plan's own SAQ A gate (docs/plan.md)

shopify.text: Native: two-step authentication and passkeys are open to every staff user, who set it up for their own account; the owner cannot activate it for others and only Plus can require a secure sign-in for all users.

gap: All four criteria are built (TOTP enrolment with ten single-use recovery codes from Your account, a challenge after the password or magic link, the owner's store requirement stores.require_two_step, platform admins always, audit entries, an atomic five-tries-in-15-minutes limit) and held by unit tests and integration tests with an injected Supabase client; getAccount() fails closed and reads enrolment from the signed aal claim or a server-side getUser(), never the cookie. Partial because no test talks to a real Supabase Auth (CI has none): enrolment, the challenge, the aal2 claim and the admin delete-factor call used by a recovery code have not been seen working, and e2e/admin-two-step.spec.ts reaches only the signed-out redirects. Not done by design: passkeys, Supabase's experimental native recovery codes, SMS. The migrations staff_security and staff_security_rules are not yet applied to production.

An owner can require two-step sign-in for the store's staff; a member without it is held at enrolment before reaching the admin. (Beyond Shopify's native, which only Plus has.)
Enrolling, removing a factor and a failed second step are written to the audit log; recovery codes are single-use.
Platform admins are required to use it. (Beyond Shopify's native, which only Plus has.)

history.why: Read src/server/two-step.ts, src/lib/two-step.ts, the account gate in src/server/auth.ts and the pages under /admin/sign-in/two-step; ran two-step.test.ts, two-step.int.test.ts, account-gate.int.test.ts, security-review.int.test.ts, store-mcp.int.test.ts (pass). shopify.text: Native (corrected from Plus). The Shopify help page for the store activity log names no plan restriction: it lists recent actions by the owner or staff in the admin (deleting a product, changing settings, granting app access), up to 250 results, view-only and not exportable. Whether Plus has a longer or exportable log was not found.

gap: Criteria 1, 2 and 4 hold and are tested; criterion 3 does not hold in the screen. activityPeople() (src/server/activity.ts), which fills the person filter on /admin/{store}/activity, takes no role into account: a member whose role lacks staff:read (the seeded Read-only role, for one) is offered every current and past member of the store by name or email, although the Team page and the log's own staff entries are refused them. Shown on 2026-10-03 with a Read-only member against a fresh database; activity.int.test.ts checks the people list for an owner only, so no test holds it. Fix: offer the person filter only the accounts that appear in the entries this viewer may see (or all of them only with staff:read or owner), and add a test with a Read-only and an orders-only member. Everything else was re-run and holds: filters, cursor paging, visibility of entries by area, store isolation, the owner-only formula-safe CSV (50,000-row cap), allowlisted changes for product, price, page, discount, shipping, staff and payment-setting writes (audit-coverage.int.test.ts calls the real server functions), append-only entries with deletion only after 24 months through the daily cron. Not applied to production until the lead applies the migrations.
criteria: An owner opens an Activity log page listing who did what and when across the store, filterable by person, area and period, paged.
Product, price, page, discount, shipping, staff and payment-setting changes each write an entry with the account and the changed fields (never secrets).
The log can be exported as CSV by owners; staff see only what their role allows; another store's entries never appear. (CSV export goes beyond Shopify's activity log, which cannot be exported.)

criteria: A paid shop order gets a legal invoice in the store's own gap-free series (seller and buyer details, VAT per rate, VAT number, payment, date) issued once by an SQL function and immutable afterwards, with a PDF and a link in the order email and account; legal means the content list for NO, SE, DK, DE and the VAT Directive's Art. 226, not another country's.
A refund or a withdrawal refund produces a credit note in its own gap-free series that references the invoice and lists the refunded lines and VAT.

Invoice and credit-note totals equal the order's less free-trial subscription lines billed at the first renewal, and the credit notes sum to the refunds up to what the invoice left uncredited (including bonus credit, group and code discounts, multi-currency), held by scenarios in checkout-kinds.int.test.ts.
Copied and host orders get none; the numbers cannot be skipped, lowered or deleted.
